info.title: Firecrawl API
info.description:
Unified API documentation for Firecrawl endpoints including Scrape, Search, Map, Parse, Crawl, and Batch Scrape. Scrape, Search, Map, and Parse are synchronous. Crawl and Batch Scrape are asynchronous: the caller submits a job and then polls the returned job resource for status and results.

Billing is metered per Firecrawl credit consumed rather than a flat per-request price, so total cost scales with the number of pages, links, or results the job produces. Approximate credit usage: Scrape = 1 credit per page, Map = 1 credit per page, Search = about 2 credits per 10 results, Crawl = 1 credit per page, Batch Scrape = 1 credit per page. The USD rate per credit depends on your tier (normal $0.005, vip $0.004, svip $0.0034).

AsyncJob.description: An asynchronous integration job. Returned by the submit call (HTTP 202) and by the poll/detail call. Poll the job by its id until status is a terminal value (completed, failed, or cancelled).

id.description: Unique AIsa job identifier. Use it to poll, list, or cancel the job.

endpoint.description: The submit endpoint this job belongs to.

status.description: Customer-facing lifecycle status. queued and running are non-terminal; completed, failed, and cancelled are terminal.

completedAt.description: When the job reached a terminal status. Null while the job is still queued or running.

authorizedMicrosUSD.description: Amount authorized (held) when the job was admitted, in micro-USD. Metered jobs settle to the actual credits consumed.

finalMicrosUSD.description: Final settled cost in micro-USD once the job is terminal. Null until settlement.

output.description: Job result payload. Present only once status is completed. For crawl this is the array of scraped pages; for batch scrape it is the array of scraped documents.

outputExpired.description: True when the result has been retained past its retention window and is no longer retrievable.

error.description: Present when status is failed. Null otherwise.

post.summary: Scrape a single page and return its main content as markdown.
post.description: Synchronous. Fetch one URL and return its cleaned main content as markdown. On the AIsa metered profile the request is restricted: the URL must be HTTPS and must not point at a PDF, proxy must be set to "basic", and if formats is supplied it must be exactly ["markdown"]. Advanced options (actions, headers, parsers, profile, lockdown, zeroDataRetention) are rejected. Billed at 1 Firecrawl credit per page scraped.

url.description: The HTTPS URL to scrape. PDF URLs are not supported on the metered profile.

proxy.description: Proxy tier. Must be explicitly set to "basic" on the metered profile.

formats.description: Optional output formats. When present it must be exactly ["markdown"].

markdown.description: The scraped page content in markdown.

metadata.description: Page metadata such as title, description, source URL, and HTTP status.

creditsUsed.description: Firecrawl credits consumed by the request (1 per page).

post.summary: Run a web search and return ranked results.
post.description: Synchronous. Search the web and return ranked results. On the AIsa metered profile only the web source is supported: scrapeOptions, enterprise mode, and non-web sources are rejected. Billed at roughly 2 Firecrawl credits per 10 results (credits = ceil(limit / 10) * 2).

query.description: The search query. Must be non-empty and at most 500 characters.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return.

post.summary: Discover the URLs on a website.
post.description: Synchronous. Given a starting URL, discover and return the links reachable on that site. The URL must be HTTPS and limit is required (1 to 100000). Billed at 1 Firecrawl credit per discovered link/page.

limit.description: Maximum number of links to discover. Required on the metered profile.

title.description: Title of the discovered page, when available.

creditsUsed.description: Firecrawl credits consumed (1 per discovered link).

post.summary: Parse an uploaded HTML file into markdown.
post.description: Synchronous. Upload a single HTML/HTM file and receive its parsed markdown. This endpoint uses multipart/form-data with two fields: file (the HTML upload) and options (a JSON string). On the metered profile options must set proxy to "basic" and may only additionally set formats to ["markdown"]. The options JSON string is limited to 64 KB. Billed at 1 Firecrawl credit.

file.description: The HTML/HTM file to parse. Must have a text/html content type or an .html/.htm filename.

options.description: JSON string of parse options. Must include proxy="basic"; may additionally include formats=["markdown"]. No other keys are allowed.

post.description:
Asynchronous. Submit a crawl of an entire site rooted at url; the whole traversal runs as a background job.

Lifecycle:
1. Submit — POST /firecrawl/crawl with the crawl body and a required `Idempotency-Key` header. On success the API returns HTTP 202 Accepted, a `Location` response header pointing at the job resource (`/apis/v1/firecrawl/crawl/{jobId}`), and an integration_async_job body with `status` = queued.
2. Poll — GET /apis/v1/firecrawl/crawl/{jobId} to retrieve the job. Repeat until `status` is terminal (completed, failed, or cancelled). When completed, the scraped pages are in `output`.
3. List — GET /apis/v1/firecrawl/crawl (optional `limit`, `status`, `cursor` query params) to page through your jobs on this endpoint.
4. Cancel — POST /apis/v1/firecrawl/crawl/{jobId}/cancel to request cancellation.

The URL must be HTTPS and not a PDF, and limit (1 to 1000) bounds the number of pages. Billed at 1 Firecrawl credit per page crawled; total cost scales with the pages actually processed.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Unique key (1 to 191 characters) that makes the submit idempotent. Re-submitting with the same key returns the original job.

url.description: The HTTPS root URL to crawl. PDF URLs are not supported.

limit.description: Maximum number of pages to crawl.

includePaths.description: Only crawl URLs whose path matches one of these patterns.

excludePaths.description: Skip URLs whose path matches one of these patterns.

maxDiscoveryDepth.description: Maximum link-discovery depth from the root URL.

sitemap.description: How the site's sitemap is used during discovery.

ignoreQueryParameters.description: Treat URLs that differ only by query string as the same page.

crawlEntireDomain.description: Crawl the whole domain rather than only the subtree under the root URL.

allowSubdomains.description: Follow links into subdomains of the root domain.

delay.description: Delay in seconds between requests (0 to 30).

maxConcurrency.description: Maximum number of concurrent page fetches (1 to 20).

scrapeOptions.description: Per-page scrape options applied while crawling. On the metered profile output is always markdown.

onlyMainContent.description: Return only the main content of each page.

maxAge.description: Maximum acceptable cache age in milliseconds.

minAge.description: Minimum cache age in milliseconds before a page is refetched.

202.description: Crawl job accepted. The Location header points at the job resource; poll it until terminal.

Location.description: Path of the created job resource, e.g. /apis/v1/firecrawl/crawl/{jobId}.

get.description: Retrieve a previously submitted crawl job. Repeat until `status` is terminal (completed, failed, or cancelled). When completed, the crawled pages are in `output`.

parameters.name: jobId
parameters.description: The job id returned by the submit call.

200.description: The current state of the crawl job.

post.summary: Submit an asynchronous batch scrape job.
post.description:
Asynchronous. Scrape many URLs in one background job.

Lifecycle:
1. Submit — POST /firecrawl/batch-scrape with the batch body and a required `Idempotency-Key` header. On success the API returns HTTP 202 Accepted, a `Location` header pointing at the job resource (`/apis/v1/firecrawl/batch-scrape/{jobId}`), and an integration_async_job body with `status` = queued.
2. Poll — GET /apis/v1/firecrawl/batch-scrape/{jobId} until `status` is terminal (completed, failed, or cancelled). When completed, the scraped documents are in `output`.
3. List — GET /apis/v1/firecrawl/batch-scrape (optional `limit`, `status`, `cursor` query params).
4. Cancel — POST /apis/v1/firecrawl/batch-scrape/{jobId}/cancel.

Every URL must be a unique HTTPS URL and must not be a PDF; 1 to 1000 URLs per job. Billed at 1 Firecrawl credit per page scraped; total cost scales with the pages actually processed.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Unique key (1 to 191 characters) that makes the submit idempotent. Re-submitting with the same key returns the original job.

urls.description: 1 to 1000 unique HTTPS URLs to scrape. PDF URLs are not supported.

maxConcurrency.description: Maximum number of concurrent scrapes (1 to 20).

onlyMainContent.description: Return only the main content of each page.

maxAge.description: Maximum acceptable cache age in milliseconds.

minAge.description: Minimum cache age in milliseconds before a page is refetched.

202.description: Batch scrape job accepted. The Location header points at the job resource; poll it until terminal.

Location.description: Path of the created job resource, e.g. /apis/v1/firecrawl/batch-scrape/{jobId}.

get.description: Retrieve a previously submitted batch scrape job. Repeat until `status` is terminal (completed, failed, or cancelled). When completed, the scraped documents are in `output`.

parameters.name: jobId
parameters.description: The job id returned by the submit call.

200.description: The current state of the batch scrape job.
